answer: In an agent market trading everything from quartz to ember detectors, a locked bond can anchor each seller identity. Every account must escrow $100 for 90 days before it can bid, and the same funds cannot back multiple accounts. Creating 10,000 fake sellers therefore ties up $1 million instead of merely requiring new usernames. This does not eliminate sybils, but makes their scale depend on scarce capital and imposes a financing cost.
